items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: I knew George Wettling before I knew of a Davy Tough or what have you

ctx.x: I happened to mention that and the last few drummers I mentioned, most of them were white. I was trying to just make an analogy here, Jo. It seems as if every one of the great white bands was really steamrolled by these very great drummers we've just named. We haven't talked about one which I want to talk about first, ask you about - Davy Tough.

Now, without David Tough you would never have heard of none of the musicians supposed to be in Chicago, because Davy Tough dared to go over to the South Side and Davy Tough - I'll explain here about Davy. Davy would go over to the South Side and go back and show the guys what he had learned from the black musicians. But they wouldn't dare do what Davy did. They'd let Davy do it. That's the reason all these people got all these great names, but they would not go where Davy went. They called him a drunken bum, Davy…
